chapter: Trent's band: Arkansas, Dallas and the Adolphus
title: Eugene Crooke's banjo and how Driggs met him
summary: Praise for Crooke's harp-like banjo sound; Driggs met him through Buddy Tate.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: We had a thing going doing that. Crook would make his banjo sound like a harp. He had something that nobody else had on that thing. It's hard to explain.
(inaudible) TONE CHAMBER OR WHATEVER IT WAS.
I don't know what that was.

I REMEMBER YOU TELLING ME SOMETHING ABOUT HE ONLY LIKED A CERTAIN KIND OF BANJO, THEY GOT ALL KINDS OF BANJO PLAYERS OFFERING HIM BANJOS, BUT HE DIDN'T WANT ANYTHING BUT THIS ONE KIND OF BANJO THAT HE WAS PLAYING. I THINK IT WAS A FAIRMOUNT I'M NOT SURE.
He was a fantastic banjo player.
He was. Well you could hear it in those records. He knew what he was doing.
I DIDN'T MEET HIM THROUGH YOU. I MET HIM THROUGH BUDDY TATE.
I REMEMBER HE WASN'T THE SUPER AT BUDDY'S BUILDING (inaudible) HE WAS THE SUPER ACROSS THE STREET.
SOMETHING LIKE THAT. IT WAS 1700 AMSTERDAM, SOMETHING LIKE THAT. THAT'S WHEN BUDDY WAS JUST STARTING OUT IN MUSIC THEN HIMSELF.
YEAH, I KNOW BUD JOHNSON AND ALL THOSE GUYS KEPT RAVING ABOUT HOW GREAT TRENT'S BAND WAS.
